question: What's the right way to win back a customer who churned 30 days ago to a competitor at half the price?
answer:
## Direct Answer Price-only churn is often symptom, not cause. Win-back requires diagnosing root issue (product gap, support failure, usability) and creating **time-bound** re-engagement with measurable value prop, not just a discount match. --- ## Operator's Playbook ### Phase 1: Diagnosis (Days 1–3) - **Exit interview substitute**: Use Gainsight or Totango to surface last activity, feature adoption, support tickets. Did they contact your team before leaving? - **Competitor intel**: Research what **half-price** actually gets them. Document feature gaps vs. your platform. - **Segmentation question**: Was this a net-negative account (high support cost, low expansion), or a real loss? ### Phase 2: Value Reposition (Days 4–7) Create a **structured re-engagement campaign** (not just a discount email): | Touchpoint | Approach | Owner | ROI Signal | |---|---|---|---| | Email 1 (Day 3) | Acknowledge churn, surface 1 specific product win they missed | CRO | Open rate >35% | | Call (Day 5) | Honest conversation: why'd you leave? What would bring you back? | CSM/AE | Genuine feedback | | Email 2 (Day 8) | Time-bound offer: **free 30-day trial** + 1 feature unlock (e.g., API access), expires Day 38 | RevOps | Click rate >20% | | Warm intro (Day 10) | Executive peer call (your CFO to their CFO) if **ARR >$50K** | Executive | Credibility | ### Phase 3: Retention Gate (Post-Win) If they re-sign: - **Lock in** via Bridge Group methodology: assign dedicated CSM, schedule **bi-weekly** check-ins. - **Gainsight health score**: Monitor adoption 2x weekly for **60 days**; flag red flags at day 15, 30. - **Pavilion playbook**: Document why they churned—feed back to product (feature request) + sales (pitch gap). ### Metrics to Track - **Win-back rate**: Target **15–25%** of churn cohort within 90 days - **Net discount offered**: Avoid ≥40% reduction; instead: free tier + service add-on - **Time to decision**: Track how long from outreach to re-engage (benchmark: **14 days**) - **Churn-back risk**: 2/3 of win-backs churn again within 12 months; use **OpenView** post-win engagement scores --- ## Churn Win-Back Decision Flow ```mermaid graph TD A[Customer Churned] --> B{Was this a

Competitor at half cost likely has: - Lower feature set (a *real* advantage for simple use cases) - Weaker support (often acceptable if product is intuitive) - No road map (your differentiator) Your win-back should emphasize: *
